psychological_angle: How constant social observation flattens authentic cognition into an internal performative habit.
logline: In a town where every passing thought can be heard, the kindest man alive lets one honest thought slip, and discovers that a mind which is always listened to may never have been his own.

author_brief.protagonist: Thomas Wren, 56, the town baker, short grey beard, white flour-dusted apron, sleeves rolled. His thoughts have been the gentlest in town for thirty years. Wound: punished as a boy for a cruel thought he never acted on. Desire: to be good all the way through. Inner belief: "If my thoughts are clean, I am clean."
other_characters: Nell Wren, 54, his wife of 26 years, seamstress, long silver braid, dark green wool coat. Calm, warm, always pleasant thoughts. She has a private life he knows nothing about.
Townsfolk: never named, only a few soft background figures in the bakery.
author_brief.setting: Wickham's Rest, an isolated stone town on the English moors, timeless present, no phones on screen. The rule: inside the town, anyone within a few steps hears your surface thoughts as a quiet voice. Beyond the old boundary stones on the moor ("the Line"), there is silence. Never explained. Locations: the bakery at dawn, the Wrens' kitchen at night, the boundary stones under a cold sky.

beats.hook: dawn, a queue in the bakery. Thomas hands over a loaf, and a thought escapes him that everyone hears: "I don't want to be here." The room goes silent: nobody has ever heard Thomas think anything unkind.
beats.strategy_works: the town lives by "clean thinking". Children learn to think gently; there is no lying, no crime, and Thomas and Nell have never argued in 26 years. Next morning he thinks warm, perfect thoughts, and the queue forgives him.
beats.hidden_cost: now he can hear the effort. An editor in his head rewrites every thought before it forms, and he hears the same editor in everyone. At supper Nell thinks "what a lovely evening" while her face looks exhausted. He starts walking to the Line at night.
beats.reversal: beyond the stones, in total silence, Thomas waits for his real thoughts to arrive. Nothing comes, only the same gentle sentences, even with no one to hear them. Then footsteps: Nell crosses the Line behind him. Unable to hear each other for the first time, she speaks aloud: "I've been coming here for years." He has never known her, only her clean thoughts, and she has only known his.
beats.philosophical_layer: Are we our thoughts, or what we do with them? Is a kindness you are forced to think still yours? Maybe a self needs a place where no one is listening.
beats.ending: they stand in the dark beyond the stones. Nell asks quietly: "What do you actually think, Thomas?" A long silence; he opens his mouth. Cut before he answers. One final narrated line turns the question to the viewer, without explaining it: "There is a thought in your head right now that no one will ever hear. Is that one you, or is the one keeping it quiet?"

author_brief.tone: Quiet, intimate, unsettling, contemplative. The dread is inward: viewers keep testing themselves ("what would I have thought?") through Thomas, never through lectures. Let key lines breathe.
must_include: the slipped thought in the bakery queue, heard by everyone
heard thoughts as quoted inner lines, quieter than speech
the "editor" Thomas notices in his head
Nell's pleasant thought contradicting her tired face
the boundary stones and the silence beyond them
must_avoid: villains, violence, crime or a mob turning on Thomas
death or grief as a central theme
visible text, glowing words or symbols in images to show thoughts
a neat resolution or revealing what Thomas answers

title_candidates.title: In This Town, Everyone Can Hear Your Thoughts
He Kept His Thoughts Clean for 26 Years
title_candidates.rationale: Anchors in a concrete time span and introduces curiosity about why someone would curate their thoughts.

title_candidates.title: He Lived 30 Years Where Everyone Heard His Thoughts
title_candidates.rationale: Establishes the core speculative rule immediately through an individual's decades-long experience.

title_candidates.title: He Crossed the Line to Think Alone for the First Time
title_candidates.rationale: Focuses on the pivotal reversal moment of seeking complete cognitive isolation beyond the town boundary.

title_candidates.title: His Wife Followed Him Beyond the Line in the Dark
title_candidates.rationale: Highlights the dramatic turning point between Thomas and Nell in the unmonitored silence of the moors.

title_candidates.title: The Man Who Never Had an Unkind Thought
title_candidates.rationale: Presents an unsettling character profile that invites the audience to question if such purity is possible.
